title: Physio-Control LIFEPAK 15 Defibrillator - Error: TH_ERROR_SHOCK_NOT_DELIVERED Shock Not Delivered
description: This guide helps troubleshoot TH_ERROR_SHOCK_NOT_DELIVERED when the Physio-Control LIFEPAK 15 reports that a shock was not delivered or therapy output may not have occurred.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Immediately remove the LIFEPAK 15 from patient use if this error occurs during therapy, testing, or operational checkout. Use another verified defibrillator for patient care. Do not attempt repeated shock delivery on a patient with a device that has reported a shock delivery failure. Expected outcome: Patient care continues with a known functional defibrillator.

steps.title: Verify the Reported Error and Behavior
steps.instructions: Confirm the exact reported error is TH_ERROR_SHOCK_NOT_DELIVERED. Confirm whether the associated therapy service code is a00b. Document whether the error occurred during manual defibrillation, synchronized cardioversion, AED mode, operational checkout, bench testing, or intermittently after a charge or discharge attempt. Look for symptoms such as shock not delivered, charge completed but no discharge occurred, therapy event aborted, service indicator present, therapy service code recorded, unexpected audible tone or message, or failure during defibrillator output verification. Expected outcome: The error is reproducible, clearly observed, or confirmed in the service or event log.

steps.title: Remove the Device From Service
steps.instructions: Do not return the device to clinical use after simply clearing the message or power cycling the unit. Label the LIFEPAK 15 as Out of Service. Expected outcome: The device is prevented from being used for patient therapy until corrective action and verification are completed. Why it matters: A defibrillator that reports shock not delivered cannot be trusted for emergency therapy until delivered-energy performance is verified.

steps.title: Check External Therapy Setup During Controlled Testing Only
steps.instructions: Perform checks in a controlled bench environment using approved test equipment, not on a patient. Inspect the therapy cable connection at the defibrillator. Confirm the cable is fully seated, latched, and not loose. Expected outcome: The therapy cable is secure with no visible connector damage.

steps.title: Inspect the Therapy Cable
steps.instructions: Check the therapy cable for cuts, crushed sections, bent pins, loose connector strain relief, contamination, fluid intrusion, burn marks, excessive wear, or intermittent connection when flexed. If damage is found, remove the cable from service. Retest the defibrillator only with a known-good compatible therapy cable and proper test load. Expected outcome: The cable is physically intact and suitable for controlled testing, or the defective accessory is removed from use.

steps.title: Verify Electrodes or Test Load Setup
steps.instructions: For bench testing, connect the LIFEPAK 15 to an appropriate defibrillator analyzer or approved test load. Confirm the correct adapter is used. Confirm pads, paddles, or the appropriate therapy adapter are properly connected. Confirm the test load is compatible and the analyzer is set up correctly. Confirm no loose or open connections are present. Expected outcome: The defibrillator sees a valid therapy load during controlled testing.

steps.title: Check for Accessory-Related Failure
steps.instructions: If facility policy allows, repeat controlled testing using a known-good therapy cable. Use known-good pads, paddles, or therapy adapter as applicable. Use a known-good defibrillator analyzer or test load connection. If the error clears with replacement accessories, remove the failed accessory from service. Complete required defibrillator output testing before returning the LIFEPAK 15 to use. Expected outcome: The error does not follow a defective cable, adapter, electrode set, or test load setup.

steps.title: Check Power and Battery Condition
steps.instructions: Verify the unit is connected to a known-good power source or has a known-good charged battery installed. Inspect battery contacts and battery seating. Watch for power instability during charge and discharge testing. Expected outcome: Device power remains stable during controlled charge and discharge testing.

steps.title: Review Related Service Indicators or Therapy Codes
steps.instructions: Check for additional service indicators, repeated therapy service codes, or related defibrillation and pacing errors. Document whether TH_ERROR_SHOCK_NOT_DELIVERED appears alone or with other therapy-related errors. Expected outcome: Any related service-code pattern is captured before escalation.

steps.title: Perform Controlled Defibrillator Output Verification After Corrective Action
steps.instructions: After any accessory correction or repair action, perform required defibrillator delivered-energy testing using approved test equipment and facility procedure. Verify that the LIFEPAK 15 can charge properly. Verify that the LIFEPAK 15 can disarm properly. Verify that the LIFEPAK 15 can deliver shock into the test load. Verify that the LIFEPAK 15 records the therapy event correctly. Verify that delivered-energy performance requirements are met. Expected outcome: Delivered-energy testing passes before the unit is returned to service. Do not return the LIFEPAK 15 to service based only on normal startup or absence of the error message.

steps.title: Stop When Resolved
steps.instructions: If the error is traced to a defective external accessory, remove that accessory from service. Complete and pass required operational, therapy, and delivered-energy testing. Return the LIFEPAK 15 to service only after the unit passes all required checks. Expected outcome: The device is safe, functional, and documented before clinical release.

CCR.Complaint: LIFEPAK 15 reported TH_ERROR_SHOCK_NOT_DELIVERED with therapy service code a00b. Staff reported shock was not delivered during therapy attempt or operational checkout.
CCR.Cause: External therapy setup was inspected. Therapy cable, electrodes or test load, power source, and controlled test setup were checked. Error indicates shock delivery failure; persistent condition suggests internal therapy subsystem fault if not resolved by accessory correction.
CCR.Resolution: Removed LIFEPAK 15 from service and labeled Out of Service. Verified therapy cable, electrode, and test load setup during controlled bench testing. Device escalated for corrective action and defibrillator delivered-energy testing prior to return to service.

title: Physio-Control LIFEPAK 15 Defibrillator - Error: TH_ERROR_CHARGING_EXPIRED Charging Time Expired
description: Troubleshooting TH_ERROR_CHARGING_EXPIRED on the Physio-Control LIFEPAK 15 when the defibrillator cannot complete charging within the expected time, which may affect therapy readiness or shock delivery.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: If the LIFEPAK 15 is connected to a patient or needed for active emergency care, remove it from patient use immediately if another defibrillator is available. Provide clinical staff with a verified replacement defibrillator before troubleshooting continues. Do not attempt to clear or evaluate a charging timeout while the device is relied on for defibrillation, cardioversion, pacing, or monitoring. Expected outcome: Patient care continues with a known-good device.

steps.title: Verify the Reported Error and Behavior
steps.instructions: Confirm the exact error reported is TH_ERROR_CHARGING_EXPIRED. Check the service log for therapy service code a00d. Note whether the error occurred during startup, manual defibrillator charge, synchronized cardioversion setup, AED operation, or intermittent testing. Expected outcome: The error is reproducible or clearly documented in the service log.

steps.title: Translate the Error Into the Real-World Failure
steps.instructions: TH_ERROR_CHARGING_EXPIRED means the defibrillator charging process exceeded the allowed time. In practical terms, the device may be unable to charge to the selected energy level fast enough, or it may fail to complete charge readiness. Treat the reported condition as a therapy-delivery reliability issue. Expected outcome: The device is not considered safe for routine clinical use until objective testing confirms proper charging and delivered energy performance.

steps.title: Remove the Device From Service
steps.instructions: Remove the LIFEPAK 15 from clinical use. Attach an Out of Service tag and follow facility policy for sequestering critical-care equipment. Prevent the unit from being returned to crash cart, emergency department, transport, or procedural use until evaluation is complete. Expected outcome: The device is no longer available for emergency response use while the therapy charging concern is unresolved.

steps.title: Check Battery and External Power Condition
steps.instructions: Verify the installed batteries are properly seated, charged, and not damaged. If available, test with known-good LIFEPAK 15 batteries. Connect the device to a known-good power adapter or station power source if used by your facility. Look for low battery indications, abnormal shutdown behavior, poor battery retention, or power interruptions during charging attempts. Expected outcome: The unit has stable power and adequate battery condition before deeper evaluation continues.

steps.title: Inspect External Physical Condition
steps.instructions: Check the LIFEPAK 15 for obvious damage, fluid intrusion, cracked housing, missing covers, or signs of impact. Inspect therapy cable ports, paddles, pads cable, and therapy connectors for bent pins, contamination, looseness, corrosion, or damage. Confirm no accessory or connector damage appears related to the reported charging failure. Expected outcome: No external condition is found that would explain unreliable therapy operation.

steps.title: Check Therapy Accessories
steps.instructions: Inspect the therapy cable, paddles, hands-free therapy cable, and defib pads connection path. Replace questionable therapy accessories with known-good compatible accessories before bench testing. Confirm the correct test load, analyzer connection, paddles, or therapy cable setup is being used during controlled testing. Expected outcome: The charging error is not caused by a visibly damaged or incompatible external therapy accessory.

steps.title: Attempt Controlled Bench Verification Only
steps.instructions: Perform testing only in a controlled Clinical Engineering environment using appropriate defibrillator analyzer equipment and facility-approved procedures. Do not test defibrillation energy output on a patient or in an active clinical area. Confirm whether the device can charge and discharge properly at selected energy levels. Observe whether charge time is normal, delayed, intermittent, or unable to complete. Expected outcome: The device either completes charge/discharge testing normally or the charging timeout is confirmed.

steps.title: Review Service Code History
steps.instructions: Check whether therapy service code a00d occurred once or repeatedly. Look for related therapy, charge, energy, battery, capacitor, or discharge errors in the service log. Document whether the error occurred after battery changes, accessory changes, physical damage, cleaning, transport, or a prior repair. Expected outcome: The service history supports either an isolated event requiring verification or a recurring therapy system fault.

steps.title: Do Not Return to Service Based on Power Cycling Alone
steps.instructions: If the error clears after restart, continue with full therapy and defibrillator charge testing. Do not return the unit to service simply because the message disappears. Intermittent defibrillator charge failures may not appear during every startup. Expected outcome: Return to service is based on successful functional verification, not temporary error clearance.

steps.title: Stop When Resolved
steps.instructions: If external power, battery, accessory, and controlled defibrillator analyzer testing confirm normal charge time and delivered energy, document the findings and return the device to service per facility policy. If the error remains active, recurs, or cannot be confidently ruled out, continue escalation instead of returning the device to clinical use. Expected outcome: The LIFEPAK 15 passes required operational and therapy output checks before it is made available for patient care.

CCR.Complaint: Physio-Control LIFEPAK 15 reported TH_ERROR_CHARGING_EXPIRED with therapy service code a00d. Device experienced charging time expired condition and may not reliably complete defibrillator charge cycle.
CCR.Cause: Battery condition, external power, therapy accessories, and external connections checked. Persistent or logged charging timeout indicates likely internal therapy charging or defibrillator subsystem fault requiring repair evaluation.
CCR.Resolution: Removed LIFEPAK 15 from service and labeled Out of Service. Processed therapy service code a00d. Sent for repair or bench evaluation. Defibrillator charge-time and delivered-energy testing required before return to clinical use.

steps.title: Verify the Reported Error and Behavior
steps.instructions: Confirm the exact error reported is TH_ERROR_CAP_OUT_OF_RANGE. Confirm the associated therapy service code is a00f. Check whether the error appears during startup, self-test, defibrillator charge or discharge testing, service log review, or intermittently after power cycling.

steps.title: Translate the Error Into the Real-World Failure Condition
steps.instructions: TH_ERROR_CAP_OUT_OF_RANGE indicates the defibrillator therapy capacitor is being detected outside its expected range or the related calibration check has failed. In practical Clinical Engineering terms, this may present as a failed therapy service code, failed defibrillator calibration, failed operational test, charging concern, energy delivery verification concern, or device not ready for safe clinical use.

steps.title: Check Power Source and Battery Condition
steps.instructions: Install a known-good charged LIFEPAK 15 battery. If available, connect the device to a known-good power adapter or external power source per facility process. Power the unit on and observe whether the error remains.

steps.title: Inspect the Device Externally
steps.instructions: Check the LIFEPAK 15 housing, therapy connector area, battery wells, and external ports for obvious damage, contamination, fluid intrusion, corrosion, cracks, or impact marks. Document any visible damage, heat evidence, odor, contamination, or signs of impact.

steps.title: Check Therapy Cable and Paddle/Pad Connections
steps.instructions: Inspect the therapy cable, paddles, test load connection, and therapy connector for damage, bent pins, contamination, or poor seating. If a defibrillator analyzer or test load is being used, confirm the cable is fully connected and the analyzer or test load is appropriate for the test being performed.

steps.title: Review the Service Log
steps.instructions: Access and review the service log according to facility and service procedures. Confirm the presence of therapy service code a00f. Look for related therapy errors, repeated calibration failures, charging errors, or discharge test failures.

steps.title: Perform Approved External Defibrillator Testing
steps.instructions: Using approved test equipment, perform the required defibrillator operational test or performance verification allowed by your facility process. Verify whether the unit can charge, discharge, and meet expected output performance. If the test passes and the error does not return, document the findings and follow facility return-to-service requirements.

steps.title: Perform Calibration or Service Procedure Only if Authorized
steps.instructions: If your department is authorized and equipped to perform LIFEPAK 15 defibrillator calibration or service procedures, process the service log and perform the required defibrillator test or calibration procedure. Do not open the device or perform internal service unless authorized, trained, and equipped to do so.

steps.title: Stop When Resolved
steps.instructions: If the error clears after proper service log processing, required calibration, and defibrillator performance testing, return the device to service only after all facility-required checks pass. Document the final status clearly in the work order.

steps.instructions: If the LIFEPAK 15 is connected to a patient or being prepared for pacing, remove it from patient use immediately. steps.title: Verify the Reported Error and Behavior
steps.instructions: Confirm the exact error reported is TH_ERROR_PA_RATE_OUT_OF_RANGE. Check the service log for therapy service code a010. Note whether the error occurred during startup, operational check, pacing setup, or actual pacing use. Observe whether the device reports a selected pacing rate and an actual pacing rate that do not match within tolerance. Expected: The error is confirmed in the service log or reproduced during controlled testing. Why it matters: This confirms a true therapy/pacer rate control fault instead of a user setup issue.

steps.title: Remove the Device From Service
steps.instructions: Do not return the LIFEPAK 15 to clinical use after this error is confirmed. Label the unit Out of Service and follow facility policy for defibrillator removal, backup replacement, and notification. Expected: The affected defibrillator is isolated from patient care. Why it matters: This error relates to pacing output accuracy, not a simple accessory or display issue.

steps.title: Check External and Simple Causes First
steps.instructions: Inspect the device exterior, therapy cable, pacing/therapy connector, and pads connection area for obvious damage, contamination, bent pins, fluid intrusion, or loose connections. Expected: No external damage or contamination is found. If damage is found, document it and keep the device out of service. Why it matters: External damage may contribute to therapy delivery faults or may indicate the device was dropped, exposed to fluids, or mishandled.

steps.title: Verify Power Condition
steps.instructions: Confirm the device has known-good batteries installed and/or is connected to appropriate external power if testing is performed on the bench. Check for low battery, battery communication issues, or unexpected shutdown behavior. Expected: The unit powers normally without power instability. Why it matters: Therapy testing should not be interpreted from an unstable power condition.

steps.title: Confirm the Issue Is Not Accessory-Related
steps.instructions: If facility procedure allows bench evaluation, test with known-good therapy cable and appropriate test load/analyzer setup. Do not use patient pads or patient connections for troubleshooting. Expected: The error remains associated with the defibrillator/pacer system, not the external cable or accessory. Why it matters: Accessory substitution helps rule out simple external contributors before repair escalation.

steps.title: Do Not Attempt Clinical Use Testing
steps.instructions: Do not attempt to “try pacing again” on a patient or rely on the device because pacing appears to start. A pacing rate tolerance error means the selected pacing rate and actual delivered rate may not agree. Expected: Troubleshooting remains controlled and non-clinical. Why it matters: Intermittent or inaccurate pacing behavior can create direct patient risk.

steps.title: Process the Therapy Service Code
steps.instructions: Record therapy service code a010 and process the device according to facility corrective action procedure. Include the error name, selected pacing rate if available, actual measured/reported rate if available, and when the fault occurred. Expected: The fault is documented clearly for repair evaluation. Why it matters: The error parameter may help repair personnel identify whether the rate control issue is repeatable or range-dependent.

steps.title: Perform Pacer Characteristic Testing After Corrective Action
steps.instructions: After repair or corrective action, verify pacer performance using appropriate test equipment before return to service. Confirm pacing rate accuracy across required settings per facility or service procedure. Expected: Pacer rate output matches selected settings within tolerance, and required performance testing passes. Why it matters: A device with a pacing rate fault must not be returned to service based only on clearing the error message.

steps.title: Return to Service Only After Passing Verification
steps.instructions: Return the LIFEPAK 15 to clinical use only after the error is cleared, corrective action is complete, and pacer characteristic testing passes. Expected: Final status is documented as safe for use. Why it matters: Defibrillator/pacer therapy functions require objective verification before clinical release.

description: Troubleshooting TH_ERROR_PA_CURRENT_OUT_OF_RANGE on the Physio-Control LIFEPAK 15 when selected pacing current does not match actual delivered pacing output tolerance.

steps.title: Verify the Reported Error and Behavior
steps.instructions: Confirm the exact error displayed or recorded is TH_ERROR_PA_CURRENT_OUT_OF_RANGE. Confirm the associated therapy service code is a011. Review whether the error occurs during startup, pacing setup, therapy testing, service review, or performance inspection. Check whether pacing is unavailable, pacing output stops, a service indicator is present, or a therapy service code is logged. Expected: The error is reproducible or clearly documented in the service log.

steps.title: Translate the Error Into the Real-World Failure
steps.instructions: This error means the LIFEPAK 15 detected that actual pacing current output is outside tolerance compared with the selected pacing current. The error parameter may include the selected pacing current and actual measured pacing current. Expected: The device is identifying a pacing output control or monitoring problem. This is not a normal lead connection message or a basic operator-correctable pacing setup issue.

steps.title: Check for Obvious External Issues
steps.instructions: Inspect the device exterior, therapy cable, therapy connector, and pacing/defib cable connection. Look for bent connector pins, damaged cable insulation, fluid contamination, cracked housing, loose connections, impact damage, or a damaged therapy pads connector. steps.title: Check the Therapy Cable and Accessories
steps.instructions: If available, connect a known-good compatible therapy cable and appropriate test load or analyzer setup. Do not test pacing output on a patient. Expected: The device either continues to report the error or the issue follows a damaged accessory. If a damaged or incorrect cable is found, replace the accessory and retest per facility procedure. If the error clears after replacing an external accessory, return the unit only after required pacing output verification and functional checks are completed.

steps.title: Verify Power Condition
steps.instructions: Confirm the LIFEPAK 15 is connected to a stable power source or has a known-good charged battery installed. Inspect battery contacts and confirm there are no shutdowns, resets, low-power symptoms, or unrelated power faults. Expected: The device powers normally without instability. steps.instructions: Immediately remove the LIFEPAK 20 / 20e from patient use if Error 9005 is active, recurring, or found during operational testing. Provide clinical staff with another verified defibrillator before continuing troubleshooting. Do not rely on the affected device for defibrillation, synchronized cardioversion, or emergency therapy standby. Expected: Patient care is transferred to a known-good defibrillator. Why it matters: Error 9005 indicates that defibrillation is disabled, so the device cannot be considered therapy-ready.

steps.title: 2. Verify the Reported Error and Behavior
steps.instructions: Confirm the exact Service Log condition: Error 9005; Defib Disabled. Determine when the error occurs: At startup; During self-test; During operational checkout; When attempting to select or charge defibrillation energy; Intermittently after power cycling. Observe associated behavior, including: Defibrillation unavailable; Charging inhibited; Therapy function not completing; Repeated service indication; Other therapy-related errors. Expected: Error 9005 is clearly documented in the Service Log or reproduced during controlled evaluation. Why it matters: This confirms a true system-reported therapy fault rather than operator setup or accessory confusion.

steps.title: 3. Check the Power Source and Basic External Condition
steps.instructions: Inspect the device for straightforward external contributors before concluding internal failure. Check: AC power connection; Battery installation and charge state; Power cord condition; Battery compartment condition; Signs of impact, liquid intrusion, overheating, or contamination. Test with a known-good approved power source or battery when appropriate. Expected: The device powers normally and Error 9005 is not explained by an obvious external power problem. Why it matters: Basic power instability should be ruled out before escalating a therapy-control fault.

steps.title: 4. Inspect Therapy Cables and External Accessories
steps.instructions: Inspect connected therapy accessories for: Loose connections; Bent or damaged contacts; Damaged therapy cable; Contamination; Incorrect accessory setup; Evidence of fluid intrusion. During controlled bench testing, use known-good compatible accessories and the proper test equipment. Expected: External therapy accessories are confirmed serviceable. Why it matters: Although Error 9005 indicates defibrillation is disabled internally, verifying the external setup prevents misdiagnosis of a separate accessory problem.

steps.title: 5. Verify Settings and Operating Configuration
steps.instructions: Confirm the device is being tested in the intended operating mode and that the reported condition is not being confused with: Incorrect therapy mode; Energy-selection setup; AED versus manual-mode expectations; Configuration restrictions; Incomplete test setup. Expected: The operating configuration is correct and Error 9005 remains present.

steps.title: 6. Power Cycle and Recheck the Service Log
steps.instructions: Remove the device from clinical use and perform a controlled restart. After restart: Recheck for Error 9005; Review the Service Log; Note whether the error immediately returns; Determine whether defibrillation remains disabled. Do not repeatedly clear or power cycle the unit in an attempt to justify return to service. Expected: Either the error clears and full therapy testing passes, or the fault persists and requires corrective action.

steps.title: 7. Isolate the Condition as Device-Related
steps.instructions: At this point, confirm that the following have been ruled out: External power source problem; Battery seating or basic power issue; Therapy cable or accessory issue; Incorrect configuration; Test setup problem; Obvious physical contamination or damage. Expected: Persistent Error 9005 is isolated to the defibrillator itself. Why it matters: The documented corrective action for this condition is replacement of the A01 System PCB, making continued external troubleshooting unlikely to resolve a persistent fault.

steps.title: 8. Stop When Resolved
steps.instructions: If the error no longer occurs, do not return the device to service based only on successful startup. Complete the required: Defibrillation functional testing; Delivered-energy verification as applicable; Required Performance Inspection Procedure (PIP). Resolved: Return the device to service only after all required defibrillation testing and PIP checks pass.

CCR.Complaint: LIFEPAK 20 / 20e reported Service Log Error 9005, “Defib Disabled.” Defibrillation function was unavailable during controlled operational evaluation.
CCR.Cause: Verified Error 9005 persisted after checking external power, battery condition, therapy accessories, physical condition, and operating configuration. Findings indicate an internal device fault requiring A01 System PCB corrective action.
CCR.Resolution: Removed device from service and labeled Out of Service. Referred unit for qualified repair and A01 System PCB replacement. Unit not approved for return until defibrillation testing and required PIP pass.

title: Physio-Control LIFEPAK 20 / 20e Defibrillator - Error: 9007 – Shock Not Delivered
description: Troubleshooting Error 9007 when the LIFEPAK 20 / 20e reports that a requested defibrillation shock was not delivered, potentially preventing critical therapy delivery.

steps.title: 1. Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Immediately remove the LIFEPAK 20 / 20e from patient use if Error 9007 is active, recurring, or associated with failed therapy delivery. Provide clinical staff with another verified defibrillator before troubleshooting continues. Do not attempt repeated shocks on a patient to determine whether the fault will recur. Expected: Patient care continues using a known-good defibrillator. Why it matters: Error 9007 directly concerns failure to deliver defibrillation therapy.

steps.title: 2. Verify the Reported Error and Behavior
steps.instructions: Confirm the exact reported or logged condition: Error 9007 – Shock Not Delivered. Review the Service Log and determine whether the error occurred during synchronized cardioversion, manual defibrillation, after charging completed, when the SHOCK control was activated, during controlled performance testing, or intermittently. Identify whether the device charged but the shock was not delivered, the charge indication disappeared without the expected discharge, the therapy sequence was interrupted, or the error occurred repeatedly or only once. Expected: Error 9007 is confirmed in the Service Log or clearly associated with a failed shock-delivery event. Why it matters: This distinguishes a true system-reported therapy failure from incorrect setup, an incomplete charge sequence, or operator misunderstanding.

steps.title: 3. Check the Power Source and Device Condition
steps.instructions: Confirm AC power is stable when applicable. Confirm the installed battery is properly seated and adequately charged. Inspect the device for physical damage. Check for contamination or liquid intrusion. Note unusual sounds, heat, or odor. Do not continue powered testing if there is evidence of overheating, burning odor, liquid intrusion, or significant physical damage. Expected: The device has a stable power source and no obvious external condition explains the therapy failure.

steps.title: 4. Inspect Therapy Cables and Connections
steps.instructions: With the device removed from clinical use, confirm the therapy cable is fully seated, paddle connections are secure if used, and the test load connection is secure during bench evaluation. Inspect connectors for bent, damaged, contaminated, or loose conditions and inspect therapy cables for obvious cuts, crushing, or strain damage. Reconnect accessible therapy connections and repeat only approved controlled testing. Expected: Therapy connections are secure and physically intact. Why it matters: A failed or incomplete external therapy connection can resemble a shock-delivery problem and should be ruled out before assuming an internal fault.

steps.title: 5. Verify the Controlled Test Setup
steps.instructions: Confirm an approved defibrillator analyzer or test load is connected. Confirm the therapy cable matches the test setup. Confirm energy selection is intentional. Confirm synchronization is disabled unless specifically being tested. Confirm no accessory or setup condition is unintentionally inhibiting discharge. Expected: The test setup supports a valid shock-delivery evaluation. Why it matters: Incorrect test configuration can create an apparent failure that is not caused by the defibrillator.

steps.title: 6. Isolate External Accessories
steps.instructions: When compatible known-good accessories are available, substitute the therapy cable, paddle assembly if applicable, and appropriate test interface one at a time. Repeat controlled testing after each substitution. Expected: Either the error follows an accessory or remains with the LIFEPAK 20 / 20e. If replacing an external accessory resolves the condition, complete required operational and therapy testing, document the failed accessory, and return the device to service only after all required tests pass. Stop troubleshooting when the issue is resolved and verified.

steps.title: 7. Reload the Device Software
steps.instructions: If external causes and test setup issues have been ruled out and Error 9007 remains applicable, follow the authorized service process to reload the LIFEPAK 20 / 20e device software. Use only approved software, service tools, and controlled Clinical Engineering procedures. Expected: The software reload completes successfully and the device can proceed to required inspection. Why it matters: The specified corrective action for Service Log Error 9007 is to reload the device software.

steps.title: 8. Perform the Required Performance Inspection Procedure
steps.instructions: After the software reload, complete the required PIP before considering the device for clinical use. Verify defibrillator charging, shock delivery, delivered energy, therapy controls, applicable synchronized therapy functions, required alarms and indicators, and overall operational readiness. Expected: The LIFEPAK 20 / 20e passes the complete required PIP and therapy testing without recurrence of Error 9007. If the error is cleared and all required tests pass, document the repair and return the device to service.

CCR.Complaint: LIFEPAK 20 / 20e reported Service Log Error 9007 – Shock Not Delivered. Device was removed from service due to reported failure of defibrillation therapy delivery.
CCR.Cause: External power, therapy connections, test setup, and accessible accessories were evaluated with no external cause identified. Error condition required manual-specified software corrective action.
CCR.Resolution: Reloaded device software using approved service process. Completed required PIP and controlled defibrillator therapy testing. Verified charging, shock delivery, and applicable delivered-energy performance passed before return to service.

title: Physio-Control LIFEPAK 20 / 20e Defibrillator - Error: 9009 Defib Charge Time Expired
description: Troubleshooting Error 9009 when LIFEPAK 20 / 20e defibrillator charging fails to complete within the allowed interval, potentially preventing timely therapy delivery.

steps.title: 1. Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Remove the LIFEPAK 20 / 20e from patient use immediately if Error 9009 is active, recurring, or associated with delayed or failed charging. Provide clinical staff with another verified defibrillator before troubleshooting continues. Expected: Patient care is transferred to a known-good device. Why it matters: A defibrillator that cannot reliably complete charging may not deliver therapy when needed.

steps.title: 2. Verify the Reported Error and Behavior
steps.instructions: Confirm the exact Service Log error is: 9009 – Defib Charge Time Expired. Determine when the condition occurs: during startup or inspection, during manual defibrillator charging, during controlled therapy testing, or intermittently after repeated charge attempts. Observe associated behavior, such as a charge cycle that does not complete, abnormally long charging, a terminated charge attempt, or affected therapy readiness. Expected: Error 9009 is reproducible or clearly documented in the Service Log. Why it matters: Confirms a true system-reported charging timeout rather than an operator or test-setup issue.

steps.title: 3. Check the External Power Source
steps.instructions: Verify the device is connected to a known-good AC outlet when applicable. Check for a loose AC connection, damaged power cord, failed or switched-off power strip, and abnormal AC power indications. Test the outlet with a known-good method according to Clinical Engineering practice. Expected: Stable external power is available and the device powers normally. Why it matters: External power problems should be ruled out before attributing the timeout to the device.

steps.title: 4. Inspect External Cables and Physical Condition
steps.instructions: Inspect the device for loose external connections, damaged therapy cables, bent or contaminated connectors, evidence of impact or liquid ingress, and unusual heat, odor, or sound. Do not continue charging tests if there are signs of overheating, burning odor, or significant physical damage. Expected: No external damage or connection problem explains the charging failure.

steps.title: 5. Verify the Controlled Test Setup
steps.instructions: During bench evaluation, confirm the therapy test configuration is correct and approved for the inspection being performed. Check that the appropriate test load or analyzer is being used, therapy accessories are fully seated, the selected operating mode is correct, and the test sequence is not being interrupted prematurely. Expected: The charging timeout remains after setup errors are excluded. Why it matters: An incorrect test configuration can create misleading therapy-related symptoms.

steps.title: 6. Evaluate Battery Condition
steps.instructions: Error 9009 indicates that the defibrillator charging interval expired before charging completed. The manual corrective action identifies the A07 Battery as the required replacement path. Before replacement, verify any readily observable battery-related findings, including that the battery connection is secure, whether battery-related status indications are abnormal, and whether the charge-time failure is repeatable under controlled testing. If Error 9009 is confirmed, replace the A07 Battery according to approved service procedures. Expected: The error no longer recurs and defibrillator charging completes normally. Why it matters: The manufacturer corrective action specifically directs replacement of the A07 Battery for this error.

steps.title: 7. Perform Required Functional and Therapy Inspection
steps.instructions: After battery replacement, complete the required functional and therapy inspection before returning the device to service. Verify at minimum through the approved inspection process that charging completes normally, charge time is acceptable, therapy functions operate correctly, no related Service Log error recurs, and required inspection criteria pass. Expected: The LIFEPAK 20 / 20e completes required testing without Error 9009.

steps.title: 8. Stop When Resolved
steps.instructions: If replacement of the A07 Battery corrects the condition and all required functional and therapy inspections pass, document the repair, confirm final device status, and return the LIFEPAK 20 / 20e to service. Do not continue unnecessary troubleshooting once the fault is corrected and required testing is successfully completed.

CCR.Complaint: LIFEPAK 20 / 20e reported Service Log Error 9009, Defib Charge Time Expired. Defibrillator charging failed to complete within the allowed interval during evaluation.
CCR.Cause: Confirmed recurring Error 9009 after external power, connections, physical condition, and controlled test setup were checked. A07 Battery identified by manufacturer corrective action as the required replacement path.
CCR.Resolution: Removed device from service, replaced A07 Battery using approved service procedures, and completed required functional and therapy inspection. Charge cycle completed normally with no recurrence of Error 9009. Device returned to service after passing inspection.

title: Physio-Control LIFEPAK 20 / 20e Defibrillator - Error: 900b Pacing Rate Out of Tolerance
description: Troubleshooting Error 900b when LIFEPAK 20 / 20e pacing rate is outside tolerance, potentially affecting reliable pacing therapy.

steps.title: 1. Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Remove the LIFEPAK 20 / 20e from patient use if Error 900b is active, recurring, or discovered during operational testing. If pacing or defibrillation capability is clinically needed, provide staff with another verified defibrillator before continuing. Do not troubleshoot while the device is connected to or relied upon for an active patient.

steps.title: 2. Verify the Reported Error and Behavior
steps.instructions: Confirm the exact Service Log error: Error 900b; Pacing rate outside tolerance. Determine whether the condition occurs at startup, during self-test or inspection, when pacing mode is selected, during controlled pacing performance testing, or intermittently during operation. Note incorrect measured pacing rate, unavailable or unreliable pacing, Service indication, or failed performance inspection.

steps.title: 3. Check Power and Basic External Conditions
steps.instructions: Verify the device has a stable AC power source when appropriate. Confirm the battery is installed correctly and adequately charged. Inspect the AC power cord and external connections for visible damage. Power-cycle the unit only in a controlled, non-patient environment.

steps.title: 4. Inspect Pacing Accessories and Connections
steps.instructions: Inspect the therapy cable for visible damage, contamination, or poor connector seating. Verify compatible pacing electrodes or the approved test setup are being used. Confirm connectors are fully seated. Substitute a known-good compatible therapy cable or test accessory when available.

steps.title: 5. Verify Pacing Configuration and Test Setup
steps.instructions: Confirm the selected pacing rate is intentional, test equipment is properly configured, the analyzer or pacing test load is compatible and functioning correctly, and no unusual configuration or setup error is affecting the observed measurement. Repeat the pacing check under controlled conditions.

steps.title: 6. Isolate the Failure
steps.instructions: Determine whether the condition is accessory-related, configuration-related, environmental, or device-related. If known-good accessories, stable power, and correct test configuration do not resolve Error 900b, treat the condition as an internal device fault.

steps.title: 7. Follow the Corrective Action Path
steps.instructions: For persistent Error 900b, the manual corrective action is replacement of the A01 System PCB. This is a qualified service repair and should not be treated as routine external troubleshooting. After corrective action, complete required post-repair inspection procedures, verify pacing rate performance with appropriate test equipment, confirm pacing functionality across required settings, confirm the error does not recur, and complete applicable performance inspection requirements before release.

steps.title: 8. Stop When Resolved
steps.instructions: If the issue is corrected and the LIFEPAK 20 / 20e no longer logs Error 900b, produces pacing rate within specification, passes required pacing performance testing, and passes applicable post-repair inspection, document the work and return the device to service according to facility policy.

CCR.Complaint: LIFEPAK 20 / 20e reported Service Log Error 900b, indicating pacing rate outside tolerance. Pacing performance required evaluation before return to service.
CCR.Cause: Verified Error 900b under controlled testing. Power source, therapy accessories, connections, pacing configuration, and test setup were checked without resolving the condition, indicating likely internal system fault requiring A01 System PCB corrective action.
CCR.Resolution: Removed defibrillator from clinical service and labeled Out of Service for qualified repair. A01 System PCB corrective action initiated per service guidance. Pacing performance and required post-repair inspection must pass before return to use.

title: Physio-Control LIFEPAK 20 / 20e Defibrillator - Error: 900f Unable to Initialize Therapy Control
description: Troubleshooting Error 900f when therapy control initialization fails, potentially preventing reliable defibrillation or other therapy functions.

steps.title: 1. Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Immediately remove the LIFEPAK 20 / 20e from patient use if Error 900f is active, recurring, or discovered during operational testing. Provide clinical staff with another verified defibrillator before troubleshooting continues. Do not rely on the device for defibrillation, synchronized cardioversion, or pacing while therapy control initialization remains unresolved. Expected: Patient care is transferred to a known-good defibrillator. Why it matters: Failure to initialize therapy control can affect the device’s ability to manage or deliver critical therapy functions.

steps.title: 2. Verify the Reported Error and Behavior
steps.instructions: Confirm the exact Service Log error is: Error 900f; Unable to Initialize Therapy Control. Determine when the error occurs: At startup; During self-test; During operational checkout; Intermittently after power cycling; During therapy function testing. Observe for associated symptoms such as: Therapy functions unavailable; Failed startup or readiness indication; Service indication; Inability to charge or prepare therapy; Repeated error after restart. Expected: Error 900f is clearly confirmed in the Service Log or reproduced during controlled evaluation. Why it matters: This distinguishes a true therapy-control initialization failure from an operator setup issue or unrelated accessory problem.

steps.title: 3. Check Power and External Conditions
steps.instructions: Verify the defibrillator is being evaluated with a known-good power source. Check: AC power connection; Power cord condition; Battery condition and seating; Battery contacts for visible contamination or damage; Whether the error occurs on AC power, battery power, or both. Power-cycle the device once under controlled conditions and observe whether Error 900f returns. Expected: The device receives stable power and the initialization error either clears or remains reproducible. Why it matters: Unstable power should be ruled out before concluding the therapy subsystem has an internal fault.

steps.title: 4. Inspect External Therapy Connections and Physical Condition
steps.instructions: Disconnect the device from patient use and inspect accessible external therapy-related connections and accessories. Check for: Damaged therapy cable; Bent or contaminated connectors; Improperly seated accessories; Visible impact damage; Fluid intrusion evidence; Signs of overheating or unusual odor. Do not perform repeated patient-simulation attempts if the device continues reporting Error 900f. Expected: No external damage or accessory condition explains the therapy initialization failure.

steps.title: 5. Determine Whether the Error Is Persistent
steps.instructions: After external checks, restart the device and review the Service Log again. Confirm whether Error 900f: Returns immediately; Reappears during startup; Recurs intermittently; Is accompanied by additional therapy-related service codes. Expected: A persistent or recurring 900f condition is identified as device-related rather than a temporary external issue. Why it matters: Repeated therapy control initialization failure strongly supports escalation to internal corrective action.

steps.title: 6. Follow the Manual-Backed Internal Corrective Action Path
steps.instructions: For qualified Clinical Engineering personnel working within approved service procedures, the manual-backed sequence is to evaluate the internal stack connector connection. Check the stack connector only within the authorized service process and without unnecessary deeper disassembly. Expected: The connector is confirmed properly seated and free of an obvious connection problem. If correcting an identified stack connector issue clears Error 900f, proceed to required post-repair testing.

steps.title: 7. Escalate to Therapy PCB Replacement When Required
steps.instructions: If Error 900f persists after the stack connector has been properly evaluated, the manual-backed corrective action progresses to replacement of the A04 Therapy PCB. This is no longer basic troubleshooting. The device should remain: Removed from service; Labeled Out of Service; Routed for qualified bench repair. Expected: Persistent therapy control initialization failure is treated as an internal therapy subsystem fault.

steps.title: 8. Complete Performance Inspection Procedures Before Return to Service
steps.instructions: After corrective action, complete the required Performance Inspection Procedures (PIP) and applicable therapy performance testing. Verify: Startup completes normally; Error 900f does not recur; Service Log condition is appropriately processed; Defibrillation functions pass required testing; Pacing functions pass applicable testing; Device readiness indications are normal. Expected: The LIFEPAK 20 / 20e passes required inspection and therapy verification without recurrence of Error 900f. If all required testing passes, document the repair and return the device to service.

CCR.Complaint: LIFEPAK 20 / 20e reported Service Log Error 900f, “Unable to Initialize Therapy Control,” with therapy control initialization failure during startup.
CCR.Cause: Verified recurring Error 900f after confirming stable power and ruling out external cable, accessory, and visible physical causes. Internal therapy control connection or A04 Therapy PCB fault suspected per corrective action sequence.
CCR.Resolution: Removed device from clinical service and labeled Out of Service. Evaluated stack connector per approved service process. Error persisted, requiring escalation for A04 Therapy PCB corrective action and completion of PIP before return to use.

title: Physio-Control LIFEPAK 20 / 20e Defibrillator - Error: 9011 Pacer Fault
description: Troubleshooting Error 9011 Pacer Fault when the LIFEPAK 20 / 20e reports a pacing subsystem failure that may prevent reliable pacing therapy.

steps.title: 1. Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Remove the LIFEPAK 20 / 20e from patient use immediately when Error 9011 is active, recurring, or associated with questionable pacing operation. Provide clinical staff with another verified defibrillator capable of pacing before troubleshooting continues. Do not attempt troubleshooting while the device is connected to an active patient. Expected: Patient care continues with a known-good defibrillator/pacer. Why it matters: A pacer fault may affect the availability or accuracy of transcutaneous pacing therapy.

steps.title: 2. Verify the Reported Error and Behavior
steps.instructions: Confirm the exact Service Log error is 9011 – Pacer Fault. Determine whether the condition occurs during startup, during self-test or operational checkout, when PACER mode is selected, during controlled pacing performance testing, or intermittently during operation. Check for pacing unavailable, failure to initiate pacing, unexpected pacing interruption, abnormal pacing output during controlled testing, Service indication, or repeated Service Log entries. Expected: Error 9011 is clearly confirmed in the Service Log or associated with reproducible pacing behavior. Why it matters: This distinguishes a true system-reported pacer fault from electrode, cable, setup, or operator-related problems.

steps.title: 3. Check External Power and Device Condition
steps.instructions: Before assuming an internal failure, connect the device to a known-good AC power source, confirm normal power indicators, verify installed batteries are properly seated and in acceptable condition, and inspect the device for impact damage, liquid intrusion, contamination, unusual heat, odor, or other physical abnormalities. Power-cycle the device only as part of a controlled Clinical Engineering evaluation. Expected: The unit has stable power and no obvious external condition explains the fault. Why it matters: Unstable power or physical damage can complicate troubleshooting and should be identified before internal failure is concluded.

steps.title: 4. Inspect Pacing Accessories and Connections
steps.instructions: With the device removed from patient use, inspect the therapy cable, cable connectors, test adapter if used, approved pacing electrodes or controlled test load, connector pins, and strain-relief areas. Look for bent or damaged contacts, loose connections, contamination, fluid intrusion, cracked insulation, and excessive cable wear. Reseat all accessible external connections. Expected: External pacing accessories are properly connected and physically intact. Why it matters: A damaged therapy accessory may create pacing problems, although a persistent 9011 Service Log error more strongly suggests a device-related fault.

steps.title: 5. Isolate the External Accessory Path
steps.instructions: During controlled bench evaluation, substitute known-good compatible accessories when available, including a known-good therapy cable, known-good test adapter, or verified defibrillator/pacer analyzer setup. Repeat only the appropriate operational or pacing check. Expected: The Clinical Engineer determines whether the symptom follows an accessory or remains with the LIFEPAK 20 / 20e. If the error clears with a replacement accessory, correct the accessory-related problem, complete required functional and pacing verification, document the repair, and return the device to service only after all required tests pass. If Error 9011 remains, continue troubleshooting because a device-related pacer fault is increasingly likely.

steps.title: 6. Confirm Configuration and Test Setup
steps.instructions: Verify that the observed behavior is not caused by an incorrect controlled test setup. Check correct pacing mode selection, appropriate pacing rate and current settings, proper analyzer connection, correct simulated ECG input when demand pacing is evaluated, secure therapy connections, and compatible test accessories. Expected: Test configuration is correct and the fault is not caused by setup error. Why it matters: Demand pacing tests can appear abnormal when the analyzer, simulated ECG, therapy connection, or pacing configuration is incorrect.

steps.title: 7. Review the Service Log for Recurrence
steps.instructions: Review the Service Log and determine whether Error 9011 is a single historical event, repeated across multiple startups, repeated when pacing is selected, or associated with other therapy-related errors. Document the recurrence pattern before corrective action. Expected: The error history supports either an isolated event or a persistent pacing subsystem fault. Why it matters: Repeated 9011 entries strengthen the case for internal corrective action.

steps.title: 8. Follow the Manual-Backed Software Corrective Action
steps.instructions: After external causes and test setup issues have been ruled out, follow the authorized service procedure to reload the device software. Do not improvise the software process. Use the approved Physio-Control service method, required files, and applicable service documentation. After the reload, restart the device, recheck the Service Log, repeat appropriate operational checks, and evaluate whether Error 9011 returns. Expected: The pacer fault clears if the condition was caused by corrupted or abnormal device software operation. If resolved, proceed to complete pacing performance verification before considering return to service.

steps.title: 9. Verify Pacing Performance Before Release
steps.instructions: A cleared error alone is not sufficient for return to clinical use. Using approved test equipment and facility procedures, verify applicable pacing performance, including pacing rate, pacing current/output, demand pacing behavior, pacing initiation and termination, stability of pacing operation, and absence of recurring Error 9011 indications. Expected: Pacing performance is within required specifications and the error does not recur. If all required tests pass, document the corrective action and return the device to service.

steps.title: 10. Stop When Resolved
steps.instructions: If the issue is corrected by external accessory replacement, connection correction, test setup correction, or authorized device software reload, and the LIFEPAK 20 / 20e passes all required operational and pacing performance checks, clear the device for clinical use according to facility procedure, document the final verified condition, and return the device to service. Do not continue replacing parts after the fault has been corrected and performance has been verified.

CCR.Cause: Verified stable power, inspected therapy cable and external pacing connections, confirmed controlled test setup, and reproduced Error 9011. Error persisted after external causes were ruled out, indicating a device-related pacing subsystem fault.
CCR.Resolution: Removed device from service and completed manual-backed device software reload. Error persisted, so unit was labeled Out of Service and escalated for authorized A04 Therapy PCB corrective action. Pacing performance verification required before return to service.

Expected: Persistent pacing disablement with known-good external conditions isolates the problem to the device rather than accessories or configuration.

steps.title: 6. Follow the Service Corrective Action

Do not substitute repeated resets, configuration changes, or accessory replacement for the specified corrective action when Error 9017 persists. Expected: After the approved software reload, Error 9017 no longer recurs and pacing functionality is restored. Why it matters: The reported condition is a system-level pacing disablement and requires the documented corrective-action path.

steps.title: 7. Perform Required Post-Corrective-Action Inspection
steps.instructions: After corrective action, complete the required inspection and functional verification before return to clinical use. At minimum, verify pacing functionality using approved test equipment and the applicable inspection procedure. Confirm pacing mode can be selected, pacing rate control functions correctly, pacing current control functions correctly, output is detected and measured appropriately, no recurrence of Error 9017, and no unresolved Service Log or service indicator condition remains. Expected: Pacing functionality passes inspection and the device operates normally. Stop when resolved: If Error 9017 is cleared, pacing passes the required inspection, and all applicable safety and functional checks pass, document the work and return the device to service.

steps.title: 3. Check External Power and Device Stability
steps.instructions: Verify the defibrillator is operating from a known-good AC source and/or properly charged compatible batteries. Inspect for loose AC connection, weak or depleted batteries, unexpected resets, power interruptions during startup, and other power-related errors. Repeat evaluation using a stable known-good power configuration when appropriate. Expected: The unit powers normally without resets or unstable operation. Why it matters: Unstable power can complicate system-level troubleshooting and may produce misleading intermittent behavior.

steps.title: 4. Inspect External USB Connections and Accessories
steps.instructions: Disconnect any nonessential USB-connected accessory, cable, or service connection before repeating the operational check. Inspect accessible USB connections for bent contacts, physical damage, contamination, loose fit, damaged cable ends, and evidence of fluid intrusion. Do not insert damaged accessories into the device. Expected: External USB components are physically sound and securely connected when required. Why it matters: External damage should be ruled out before concluding the internal USB circuitry has failed.

steps.title: 5. Determine Whether the Error Is Accessory-Related
steps.instructions: When a USB cable or supported external connection is associated with the complaint, substitute a known-good compatible item if permitted by facility procedure. Repeat the same controlled test. Expected: The error either clears with the known-good external item or remains associated with the defibrillator. If the error clears, replace the defective external cable or accessory and complete verification testing. If Error 502b remains, continue isolation.

steps.title: 6. Review the Service Log for Related Errors
steps.instructions: Review the Service Log for repeated 502b entries, other system communication errors, power-related errors, processor or system-board errors, and errors occurring at the same timestamp or event. Document whether 502b is isolated or part of a broader pattern. Expected: The error history helps determine whether this is an isolated USB fault or evidence of a larger system issue.

steps.title: 7. Clear the Error and Perform PIP
steps.instructions: Following the applicable service process, clear the error condition or Service Log as appropriate and perform the required Performance Inspection Procedures. Closely observe for return of Error 502b, Service LED illumination, USB-related functional failure, other new Service Log errors, and any failed PIP requirement. Expected: The LIFEPAK 20 / 20e completes PIP without recurrence of Error 502b or other unresolved faults. Why it matters: The corrective sequence uses error clearing followed by PIP to determine whether the fault was transient or persistent.

steps.title: 8. Stop When Resolved
steps.instructions: If Error 502b does not recur and the device successfully completes all required PIP and functional checks, document the findings, confirm normal final device status, and return the unit to service according to facility policy. Resolved condition: The error remains cleared, required inspections pass, and no abnormal USB or system behavior remains.

CCR.Complaint: LIFEPAK 20 / 20e reported Service Log Error 502b, USB System Failed. Error was noted during startup or PIP evaluation with concern for USB system functionality.
CCR.Cause: External connections and accessible USB components inspected with no damage or loose connection found. Error cleared and PIP performed; 502b returned, indicating likely persistent internal USB system failure requiring System PCB evaluation.
CCR.Resolution: Removed defibrillator from service, labeled Out of Service, and escalated for qualified bench repair following the service corrective path, including A01 System PCB replacement if confirmed. Post-repair PIP required before return to use.

title: Physio-Control LIFEPAK 20 / 20e Defibrillator - Error: 5030 – PP USB Disconnect
description: Troubleshooting Error 5030 when the patient-parameter USB connection disconnects, potentially affecting communication with patient-parameter functions.

steps.title: 1. Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: If Error 5030 is active, recurring, or associated with loss of monitoring parameters, remove the LIFEPAK 20 / 20e from patient use. Provide clinical staff with another verified defibrillator/monitor before continuing troubleshooting. Do not troubleshoot the device while it is actively relied on for patient monitoring or emergency therapy readiness.

steps.title: 2. Verify the Reported Error and Behavior
steps.instructions: Confirm the exact Service Log error is 5030, PP USB Disconnect, Patient-parameter USB connection disconnected. Determine when the error occurs and check for associated behavior such as missing patient parameters, intermittent parameter communication, unavailable monitoring functions, service indication, or no obvious user-facing symptom despite the logged error.

steps.title: 3. Check Power Sources and Basic Device Condition
steps.instructions: Inspect the LIFEPAK 20 / 20e for secure AC power connection, proper battery installation and condition, unexpected resets or power interruptions, loose external connectors, impact damage, liquid contamination, overheating, or abnormal odor. Use a known-good power source if unstable input power is suspected.

steps.title: 4. Check External Patient-Parameter Accessories
steps.instructions: Inspect connected monitoring accessories appropriate to the installed configuration, including ECG cables, SpO₂ sensors and interface cables, NIBP hose and cuff, CO₂ accessories if equipped, and other connected patient-parameter accessories. Disconnect damaged, contaminated, or suspect accessories and substitute known-good compatible accessories one at a time when practical.

steps.title: 5. Check Connections and Configuration Behavior
steps.instructions: Confirm that accessories are fully seated, no connector is partially engaged, installed parameter functions are recognized normally, and the device configuration matches the expected hardware setup. Power-cycle the device once under controlled bench conditions and observe whether patient parameters initialize normally.

steps.title: 6. Clear the Error and Perform the Required Performance Inspection Procedure
steps.instructions: Following the applicable Physio-Control service process, record Error 5030 before clearing, clear the error as required, perform the applicable Performance Inspection Procedure or PIP, and monitor for recurrence of the Service Log error or related parameter failure.

steps.title: 7. Determine Whether the Fault Is Transient or Persistent
steps.instructions: If the device passes PIP, maintains stable patient-parameter operation, does not regenerate Error 5030, and shows no associated monitoring malfunction, document the findings and complete all required return-to-service checks. If Error 5030 returns during PIP, startup, or repeated controlled testing, treat the condition as persistent.

steps.title: 8. Isolate as an Internal Patient-Parameter Communication Fault
steps.instructions: After external accessories, power conditions, visible damage, and configuration issues have been ruled out, recurring Error 5030 strongly indicates an internal patient-parameter communication problem. The manual-backed corrective path identifies the A02 PP PCB as the replacement target when the fault persists. Do not proceed with unnecessary deep disassembly during routine field troubleshooting.

CCR.Complaint: LIFEPAK 20 / 20e reported Service Log Error 5030, PP USB Disconnect. Patient-parameter USB communication was reported disconnected, with intermittent parameter communication concern.
CCR.Cause: External power, accessories, connectors, and visible device condition checked with no external cause identified. Error 5030 recurred after clearing and PIP, indicating likely internal PP communication failure associated with the A02 PP PCB path.
CCR.Resolution: Removed device from service, labeled Out of Service, documented recurring Error 5030, and escalated for qualified bench repair and evaluation of the A02 PP PCB. Return to service pending successful corrective action and required performance testing.

title: Physio-Control LIFEPAK 20 / 20e Defibrillator - Error: 5031 – UI USB Disconnect
description: Troubleshooting Error 5031 – UI USB Disconnect when the LIFEPAK 20 / 20e loses the user-interface USB connection, potentially affecting controls or display communication.

steps.title: 1. Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: If Error 5031 is active, recurring, or associated with abnormal display or control behavior, remove the LIFEPAK 20 / 20e from patient use. Provide clinical staff with another verified defibrillator before troubleshooting continues. Do not evaluate a recurring user-interface communication fault while the device is supporting an active patient.

steps.title: 2. Verify the Reported Error and Behavior
steps.instructions: Confirm the exact Service Log error is 5031 – UI USB Disconnect. Review whether the error occurs during startup, self-test or operational checks, front-panel control use, after device movement, or intermittently during operation. Observe for unresponsive controls, display abnormalities, unexpected resets, Service indication, or otherwise normal operation with only a logged error.

steps.title: 3. Check Power and Basic External Conditions
steps.instructions: Verify the AC power source is stable, confirm the power cord and external connections are secure, evaluate battery condition if the issue occurs on battery power, inspect for impact or transport damage, and check for visible evidence of liquid intrusion, contamination, or physical damage around the user-interface area.

steps.title: 4. Check External Accessories and Operating Conditions
steps.instructions: Disconnect nonessential external accessories according to approved operating procedures and determine whether the error remains. Confirm attached cables and accessories are properly seated and are not placing unusual strain on the device. Check whether the error appears only in a particular location, on a particular power source, or after transport. Note excessive heat, moisture, contamination, or other environmental factors that may correlate with the event.

steps.title: 5. Check for Reproducibility Without Excessive Cycling
steps.instructions: With the device removed from patient use, perform a controlled restart and determine whether Error 5031 returns during startup or subsequent operational testing. Do not repeatedly power-cycle the unit in an attempt to force a temporary clear.

steps.title: 6. Clear the Error and Perform the Required Performance Inspection
steps.instructions: Follow the approved service process to clear the recorded error and perform the applicable Performance Inspection Procedure, or PIP. Monitor for recurrence of Error 5031, Service indicator activation, user-interface instability, or failed operational checks. Return the device to service only after all required inspection requirements pass.

steps.title: 7. Identify Persistent UI Communication-Path Failure
steps.instructions: If Error 5031 returns after clearing and PIP, confirm that external power, accessories, operating conditions, and obvious physical causes have been ruled out. Recognize that the reported condition specifically indicates that the user-interface USB connection disconnected. Do not continue attempting temporary resets when the error remains repeatable or recurring.

steps.title: 8. Escalate to the Manual-Backed Corrective Action Path
steps.instructions: The documented corrective sequence progresses to authorized evaluation and replacement of the W18 UI Flex Cable as applicable, re-testing and completion of the required performance inspection, and if the error persists, authorized replacement of the A05 UI PCB as applicable. These actions should be performed only by personnel authorized for internal repair under the appropriate service procedure.

steps.title: 9. Stop When Resolved
steps.instructions: If the error no longer recurs and the LIFEPAK 20 / 20e passes all required performance inspections, confirm normal startup, normal user-interface response, no active Service indication, and completion of required functional and safety checks. Return the device to service only after all required inspections pass.

CCR.Complaint: LIFEPAK 20 / 20e reported Service Log Error 5031 – UI USB Disconnect, indicating loss of the user-interface USB connection. Error occurred intermittently during startup and operational testing.
CCR.Cause: External power, physical condition, accessories, environmental factors, and basic operating conditions checked with no external cause identified. Error recurred after controlled restart and error-clear/PIP sequence, indicating likely internal UI communication-path failure.
CCR.Resolution: Removed device from service and labeled Out of Service. Escalated for authorized corrective action beginning with W18 UI Flex Cable evaluation/replacement, followed by A05 UI PCB replacement if required. Device not returned to service pending successful PIP.

title: Physio-Control LIFEPAK 20 / 20e Defibrillator - Error: 5032 Therapy USB communication connection disconnected
description: Troubleshooting Error 5032 when therapy USB communication disconnects, potentially affecting therapy subsystem communication and overall defibrillator reliability.

steps.title: 1. Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Remove the LIFEPAK 20 / 20e from patient use if Error 5032 is active, recurring, or associated with a Service indicator or failed operational testing. Provide clinical staff with another verified defibrillator before troubleshooting continues. Never troubleshoot the device while it is relied upon for active patient monitoring or emergency therapy. Expected: Patient care is not dependent on a defibrillator with an unresolved therapy communication fault. Why it matters: A communication fault involving the therapy subsystem should not be ignored on equipment relied upon for emergency therapy.

steps.title: 2. Verify the Reported Error and Behavior
steps.instructions: Confirm the exact Service Log error is Error 5032, Therapy USB Disconnect, Therapy USB communication connection disconnected. Determine whether the error occurs during startup, self-test, operational checkout, therapy testing, normal operation, or after power cycling. Check for Service indicator illumination, failed Performance Inspection Procedure, therapy function abnormalities, repeated Service Log entries, or unexpected restart or communication-related behavior. Expected: Error 5032 is confirmed in the Service Log or clearly associated with observed device behavior. Why it matters: This confirms a true system-reported therapy communication condition rather than an unrelated accessory or user setup problem.

steps.title: 3. Check External Power Conditions
steps.instructions: Inspect the device’s external power setup before assuming internal failure. Check the AC power cord condition, secure connection at the device and outlet, known-good hospital-grade outlet, battery installation and condition, and signs of intermittent power loss. When appropriate, repeat evaluation using a known-good power source. Expected: The device receives stable power without interruption. Why it matters: Unstable power can complicate troubleshooting and may create intermittent system behavior that resembles a communication failure.

steps.title: 4. Inspect External Connections and Physical Condition
steps.instructions: Inspect the LIFEPAK 20 / 20e for loose external connectors, damaged therapy cable connections, contamination, fluid intrusion evidence, impact damage, cracked housing, signs of recent drop or transport damage, and unusual heat, odor, or sound. Do not perform deep internal disassembly as part of routine field troubleshooting. Expected: No external physical condition explains or contributes to the reported fault.

steps.title: 5. Review Connected Accessories
steps.instructions: Disconnect nonessential external accessories and repeat the controlled startup or operational check as appropriate. Inspect connected items for damaged cables, bent contacts, contamination, poor seating, and intermittent connections. Expected: The error either clears or remains independently of external accessories. Why it matters: This helps separate an external connection issue from a device-level therapy communication fault.

steps.title: 6. Process the Service Log Error
steps.instructions: Document Error 5032 and any related Service Log entries. Follow the manual-backed sequence: record the error and occurrence conditions, clear the error according to approved service procedures, power cycle the device as appropriate, and perform the required Performance Inspection Procedure. Expected: The device completes the PIP without Error 5032 returning and without other therapy-related failures. Why it matters: Clearing the code alone does not prove the underlying condition is resolved. Successful performance testing is required before return to service.

steps.title: 7. Evaluate the PIP Result
steps.instructions: If the Performance Inspection Procedure passes and Error 5032 does not recur, confirm normal startup, confirm no Service indication, confirm required therapy functions pass testing, and document the completed evaluation. Resolved: If all required testing passes and the error does not return, return the device to service according to department policy. Stop troubleshooting once the condition is resolved and required verification is complete.

steps.title: 8. Determine Whether the Error Is Persistent
steps.instructions: If Error 5032 returns after clearing, reappears during PIP, recurs intermittently, is accompanied by therapy abnormalities, or prevents successful completion of required testing, treat the condition as a persistent device-level therapy communication failure. Expected: External and common causes have been ruled out, and the fault is isolated to the device. Why it matters: The manual-backed corrective path identifies persistent Error 5032 with the therapy electronics communication path rather than a normal external setup issue.

CCR.Complaint: LIFEPAK 20 / 20e reported Service Log Error 5032, Therapy USB Disconnect. Therapy USB communication connection was reported disconnected.
CCR.Cause: Verified Error 5032 in Service Log. External power, accessible connections, accessories, and physical condition were checked. Error persisted after clearing and required PIP evaluation, indicating likely internal therapy communication failure associated with the A04 Therapy PCB path.
CCR.Resolution: Removed device from clinical service and labeled Out of Service after Error 5032 recurred during evaluation. Escalated for qualified bench repair and A04 Therapy PCB corrective action. Device not approved for return to service pending successful post-repair PIP.
