title: Physio-Control LIFEPAK 12 Defibrillator - AC Power Adapter or Battery Charger Failure
description: Troubleshooting missing AC operation, batteries not charging, abnormal charger indicators, or intermittent power caused by outlets, cords, connections, batteries, or adapter failure.

steps.title: 1. Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Do not troubleshoot an unreliable power source while the LIFEPAK 12 is connected to an active patient or serving as the only available defibrillator. If the failure occurs during patient care: Confirm the monitor has adequate battery power. Obtain another verified monitor/defibrillator immediately. Transfer monitoring and therapy capability when safe. Do not continue using the device if power stability is uncertain. Expected outcome: Patient care no longer depends on equipment with an unreliable power or charging system. Continue Clinical Engineering troubleshooting only after the LIFEPAK 12 has been removed from active clinical use.

steps.title: 2. Identify the Exact Failure
steps.instructions: Document whether the complaint involves: AC adapter POWER indicator not illuminated; LIFEPAK 12 not operating from external power; BATT CHG indicator not illuminated; Battery remaining discharged; CHARGING indicator remaining on unusually long; FAILED battery indicator; Red SERVICE indicator on the AC adapter; Intermittent charging when the cable is moved; Failure of a separate battery charger or Battery Support System. Expected outcome: The problem is narrowed to incoming AC power, the adapter, its output connection, a specific battery, or the external charger.

steps.title: 3. Inspect for Damage or Unsafe Conditions
steps.instructions: Disconnect the equipment from AC power and inspect: AC power cord and plug; Adapter enclosure; DC output cable; Any single approved extension cable; LIFEPAK 12 power-adapter connector; Battery charger trays and contacts; Battery housings and terminals. Look for bent pins, cuts, crushed insulation, looseness, corrosion, contamination, unusual heat, swelling, discoloration, or burnt odor. Do not use equipment showing electrical damage, overheating, liquid intrusion, or exposed conductors. Expected outcome: No visible condition is present that requires immediate removal from service.

steps.title: 4. Verify the AC Outlet
steps.instructions: Test the outlet with an approved outlet tester or another known-good device. Confirm that: The outlet provides stable power. The plug fits securely. A switched outlet has not been turned off. A power strip, vehicle inverter, or extension arrangement is not causing the problem. Connect the adapter directly to a verified grounded outlet whenever possible. Expected outcome: The adapter receives reliable AC input. If normal operation returns, document the defective outlet or external power source and stop.

steps.title: 5. Verify the Correct Power Cord
steps.instructions: Confirm the power cord is the correct approved cord for the AC adapter and is fully seated at both ends. Substitute a known-good compatible cord when available. Physio-Control warns that an improper power cord may produce excessive leakage current. Expected outcome: The green POWER indicator illuminates and remains steady. If replacing the cord restores operation, remove the defective cord from service and stop.

steps.title: 6. Observe the AC Adapter Self-Test
steps.instructions: Connect the AC adapter to the verified outlet without connecting it to the LIFEPAK 12. The adapter should briefly illuminate its indicators during self-test and then leave the green POWER indicator illuminated. Document any abnormal condition: No indicators; Indicators do not perform the brief self-test; POWER indicator flickers; Red SERVICE indicator remains illuminated; Unusual clicking, heat, or odor. Expected outcome: The adapter completes its self-test and shows a steady green POWER indicator. A persistent red SERVICE indicator means the adapter requires service and should be removed from use immediately.

steps.title: 7. Verify the Adapter Voltage Indicator
steps.instructions: Confirm the adapter’s displayed voltage selection matches the facility’s AC supply. Do not change an incorrect voltage setting unless authorized and trained under the applicable service procedure. Connecting an adapter configured for the wrong line voltage can permanently damage it. Expected outcome: The voltage indicator corresponds to the available AC supply. If it does not, disconnect the adapter, label it Out of Service, and send it for bench evaluation.

steps.title: 8. Check the DC Output Connection
steps.instructions: Inspect and firmly reconnect the adapter’s DC output cable at the LIFEPAK 12 POWER ADAPTER connector. When an extension cable is used: Confirm it is fully seated. Inspect both ends for damage. Remove it temporarily and connect the adapter directly. Do not connect multiple output extension cables together. Excessive cable length or resistance may prevent the adapter from charging batteries or operating the defibrillator. Expected outcome: External power is recognized with a stable connection. If direct connection resolves the issue, replace the defective extension cable and stop.

steps.title: 9. Confirm the LIFEPAK 12 Charging Indicator
steps.instructions: Install at least one compatible battery, connect the AC adapter, and power on the LIFEPAK 12. Verify that the BATT CHG indicator illuminates. This indicator shows that at least one installed battery is being charged by the AC Power Adapter. Gently check the connector for obvious looseness without stressing or repeatedly flexing the cable. Expected outcome: The BATT CHG indicator remains illuminated without interruption. If charging cuts in and out when the connector is lightly touched, remove the adapter and defibrillator from service for connector and cable evaluation.

steps.title: 10. Interpret the Adapter Battery Indicators
steps.instructions: For each installed battery position, observe: READY, green: Battery is fully charged. CHARGING, amber: Battery is charging. FAILED, red: Battery should be removed and recycled according to facility procedure. SERVICE, red: The AC adapter requires service. The LIFEPAK 12 AC adapter charges one installed battery at a time, so both battery positions may not display CHARGING simultaneously. Expected outcome: Indicator behavior corresponds logically to the installed batteries.

steps.title: 11. Isolate the Batteries
steps.instructions: Test one battery at a time in each battery well. Use a known-good, compatible, adequately discharged battery when available. Determine whether: One battery repeatedly produces a FAILED indication. All batteries fail in one battery well. One battery charges normally while another does not. No known-good battery charges in either position. Also verify battery compatibility. Some LIFEPAK NiCd 2.4 Ah batteries require an AC adapter specifically labeled as compatible. Expected outcome: The fault is isolated to a battery, battery position, compatibility issue, or the charging system. If only one battery fails, remove that battery from service and stop after confirming normal operation with a known-good battery.

steps.title: 12. Evaluate a Separate Battery Charger
steps.instructions: When the complaint involves an external battery charger or Battery Support System: Verify its outlet and approved power cord. Inspect the battery tray and contacts. Confirm the correct tray is installed for the battery type. Test one known-good battery at a time. Compare behavior across available charging bays. Record all charger status or fault indicators. The LIFEPAK 12 AC Power Adapter charges installed batteries but does not perform full battery maintenance; battery maintenance requires the appropriate Battery Support System. Expected outcome: The problem is isolated to the battery, charger tray, individual bay, or charger assembly.

steps.title: 13. Perform a Controlled Operational Check
steps.instructions: After correcting an external issue: Install verified batteries. Connect the AC adapter. Confirm normal POWER and charging indicators. Power on the LIFEPAK 12. Verify stable operation without unexpected shutdown. Disconnect AC power and confirm an orderly transfer to battery operation. Reconnect AC and confirm charging resumes. Complete the facility-approved performance and electrical-safety testing before return to service. Wait at least two seconds between disconnecting the power adapter and powering on the defibrillator to avoid a potentially misleading SERVICE indication. Expected outcome: The device operates reliably on external power and batteries, transitions correctly between sources, and passes required testing. If the issue is resolved, return the device to service according to department policy and stop.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the LIFEPAK 12 would operate on batteries but did not show the BATT CHG indicator when connected to its AC adapter.
CCR.Cause: Inspection found an intermittent DC output cable connection, and charging stopped whenever the damaged cable was lightly moved.
CCR.Resolution: Removed the AC adapter from service, installed a verified replacement adapter, confirmed normal POWER and BATT CHG indicators, and completed operational and electrical-safety testing.

title: Physio-Control LIFEPAK 12 Defibrillator - Self-Test, Startup, or Service Indicator Failure
description: Troubleshooting failed startup checks, unsuccessful User Tests, illuminated Service LEDs, maintenance messages, or abnormal startup behavior caused by power, accessories, or internal faults.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Do not troubleshoot a LIFEPAK 12 with an active Service indicator or uncertain startup condition while it is connected to a patient. If the problem occurs during patient care: Obtain another verified monitor/defibrillator immediately. Transfer monitoring, pacing, and defibrillation capability to the replacement device. Continue patient care according to the facility’s emergency-response protocol. Do not delay therapy while repeatedly restarting or testing the affected device. Expected outcome: Patient care continues without relying on a defibrillator whose readiness cannot be confirmed. Continue Clinical Engineering troubleshooting only after the LIFEPAK 12 has been removed from active patient use.

steps.title: Identify the Exact Failure
steps.instructions: Power on the device in a controlled, nonclinical area and document: Whether the display completes startup; Whether the Service LED illuminates; Whether the device restarts, freezes, or shuts down; Any displayed warning or error message; Whether an audible alert occurs; Whether the complaint involves an automatic startup self-test or a manually initiated User Test; Whether a printed User Test report shows PASS or FAIL. The LIFEPAK 12 performs internal self-tests each time it is powered on. A detected failure causes the Service LED to illuminate. Expected outcome: The failure is clearly defined before components are exchanged or the device is escalated.

steps.title: Distinguish a Maintenance Reminder From a Failure
steps.instructions: Check whether the display shows MAINTENANCE DUE without an illuminated Service LED or other malfunction. The maintenance reminder can be configured by service personnel for 3-, 6-, or 12-month intervals. It indicates that scheduled maintenance is due and does not, by itself, identify a failed startup self-test. Review the device’s maintenance history. Confirm whether preventive maintenance is overdue. Schedule the required inspection and performance verification. Do not clear or disregard the message without documenting the maintenance status. Expected outcome: A scheduled-maintenance notification is not incorrectly diagnosed as an internal device failure.

steps.title: Inspect the Device Externally
steps.instructions: Turn the device off and inspect for: Cracked housing or evidence of impact; Liquid intrusion or contamination; Damaged battery wells; Bent, recessed, corroded, or contaminated battery pins; Loose external connectors; Unusual heat, odor, or sounds; Damaged power-adapter cable or connector. Do not force batteries into the wells. Physio-Control warns that dropped or forced batteries may damage the battery pins and contribute to loss of power. Expected outcome: No external damage or contamination is found that could interfere with startup or power stability. If there is evidence of liquid intrusion, overheating, burning odor, or significant physical damage, stop troubleshooting and remove the device from service.

steps.title: Verify Battery Condition and Installation
steps.instructions: Remove both batteries and inspect them for: Cracks, swelling, leakage, or damaged contacts; Contamination on the battery terminals; Incorrect seating or incomplete engagement; Failed or abnormal battery status indicators; Overdue conditioning, testing, or replacement. Install two known-good, fully charged, compatible batteries. Ensure each battery locks securely into its well. Power on the LIFEPAK 12 and observe whether startup completes normally. Physio-Control identifies improper battery maintenance as a potential cause of power failure without warning. Expected outcome: The device starts normally using verified batteries, without the Service LED illuminating. If replacing or reseating the batteries resolves the issue, complete an operational verification, document the battery-related cause, and stop.

steps.title: Test Each Battery Position
steps.instructions: Using known-good batteries: Operate the device from battery well 1. Observe startup and the battery symbol. Repeat using battery well 2. Gently verify that normal handling does not cause restarting or loss of power. Do not manipulate the batteries aggressively or attempt to bend battery contacts. Expected outcome: The LIFEPAK 12 starts consistently from either battery position. If the failure occurs only in one battery well, remove the device from service for bench evaluation of the affected battery interface.

steps.title: Check External Power Operation
steps.instructions: When the approved LIFEPAK 12 AC Power Adapter is available: Inspect the AC cord, adapter, and DC output cable. Connect the adapter directly to a known-good outlet. Confirm that the adapter’s POWER indicator illuminates. Confirm that the DC connector is fully seated. Power on the LIFEPAK 12 and observe the Service LED and startup sequence. Confirm that the battery-charging indicator operates when compatible batteries are installed. The manufacturer’s power-adapter check calls for confirming the adapter POWER light, verifying that the LIFEPAK 12 powers on without its Service LED, and confirming battery charging indication. Expected outcome: The device starts normally from approved external power and displays normal charging indications. If the adapter’s own Service indicator is illuminated, the adapter requires qualified service evaluation.

steps.title: Remove Nonessential External Accessories
steps.instructions: With the device powered off, disconnect nonessential accessories that could affect initialization, including: ECG patient cable; SpO₂ sensor or extension cable; NIBP hose; EtCO₂ FilterLine; Invasive-pressure cables; Data or transmission accessories; Therapy cable, when appropriate for controlled testing. Leave only the verified power source connected, then restart the device. Reconnect accessories individually while observing startup behavior. Expected outcome: The LIFEPAK 12 starts normally with accessories removed. If the Service LED or startup failure returns only when one accessory is connected, substitute a known-good compatible accessory. Remove the defective accessory from service if the problem follows it.

steps.title: Perform a Controlled Power Cycle
steps.instructions: Turn the LIFEPAK 12 off. When changing between AC or DC line power and battery operation, allow at least two seconds before powering the device back on. This gives the device time to transition to battery power. Restart the unit and observe: Display initialization; Indicator lights; Audible startup tones; Battery symbols; Service LED status; Any error messages. Expected outcome: Startup completes without an abnormal indicator or repeated restart. A single transient Service indication may clear after a controlled restart. If the Service LED remains illuminated or returns, continue to the User Test.

steps.title: Perform the LIFEPAK 12 User Test
steps.instructions: Perform this test only in a nonclinical area with the device removed from patient service. Install fully charged, verified batteries. Load printer paper. Power on the device. Press OPTIONS. Select USER TEST. Allow the test to finish without interrupting it. Review the printed Pass/Fail report. The User Test performs internal self-tests, charges to 10 joules, discharges the energy internally, and prints a Pass/Fail report. Front-panel controls other than ON are disabled during the test. Expected outcome: The report prints PASS, and the Service LED remains off. If the test passes and the original problem cannot be reproduced, complete additional functional verification before returning the device to service.

steps.title: Evaluate a Failed or Interrupted User Test
steps.instructions: If the User Test does not complete: Confirm adequate battery charge. Confirm that the device did not lose power. Check that printer paper is correctly installed. Repeat the test once using verified batteries and minimal external accessories. Do not repeatedly run the test if the Service LED remains illuminated. Turning the device off during the User Test interrupts the process, and no Pass/Fail report is printed. If the report indicates FAIL, preserve the printout with the work order. Expected outcome: A valid test result is obtained without power interruption.

steps.title: Complete External Functional Verification
steps.instructions: If the User Test passes and the Service LED remains off: Confirm stable operation on battery power. Confirm stable operation on approved external power, when equipped. Verify display, controls, printer, alarms, and installed monitoring parameters. Perform approved simulator and defibrillator-analyzer testing according to facility procedures. Confirm no Service indicator returns during testing. Testing involving delivered defibrillation energy must be performed only by qualified personnel using an approved analyzer, simulator, or test load. The manufacturer warns that improperly performed discharge testing can cause serious injury or death. Expected outcome: The device completes startup, User Test, and applicable performance verification without recurring faults. If all testing passes, return the device to service according to facility policy and document the final status.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the LIFEPAK 12 illuminated the Service LED during startup and printed a failed User Test report.
CCR.Cause: The Service indication remained present after installing verified batteries, disconnecting external accessories, and repeating the User Test.
CCR.Resolution: Removed the LIFEPAK 12 from service, labeled it Out of Service, provided a replacement defibrillator, and forwarded the unit and failed test report for bench repair.
